chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Naysābūrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from Abū Naṣr Ẓarīf al-Khādim,

key_terms.أَبِي نَصْرٍ ظَرِيفٍ الْخَادِمِ: The servant named as the final narrator in this report.
key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ: A named transmitter in the lineage-based chain of narration.
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ النَّيْسَابُورِيّ: A transmitter in the chain identified by his Nisbah to Naysābūr.
key_terms.رَآهُ: He saw him; the central claim establishing direct sighting.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى: A narrator at the beginning of the sanad/isnad.

ai.seo_question: Who are the individuals named in al-Kāfī as having seen him عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report records a chain of narrators ending with Abū Naṣr Ẓarīf al-Khādim and states that he saw him. In the context of the chapter, it serves as a biographical identification of one of those who had the honor of seeing him عليه السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Al Hassan Bin Al Al Neyshapouri, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Musa Bin Ja’far, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Nasr Zareyf, the servant
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Naysaburi from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah ibn Musa ibn Ja’far from abu Nasr Zarif, the servant (of abu Muhammad (a.s.)
who has said that he saw him (the twelfth Imam (a.s.) .
